For Gaurav Kapoor’s portfolio

Three moves for Indegene across these seven accounts.

Products are launching or changing labels, governments are rewriting the price of access, and several companies are managing a breach, a settlement or a halted trial. Each opens a different door — this issue shows which one to knock on.

Three plays for this quarter

01

Launches and label changes: be in place before the rollout

What’s happeningRegeneron has PASATRU approved, Genentech has Enspryng under Priority Review in MOGAD, Pfizer has an updated COMIRNATY cleared in the US and Canada, Amgen's IMDELLTRA label cuts monitoring time, Incyte is registering OPZELURA in Australia, and J&J has two MedTech clearances.
What to doWork back from each approval or label change and open the conversation 60–90 days ahead: payer and HEOR evidence, medical and training content, field enablement, and patient-support operations. Where a label changes the setting of care, lead with site-of-care planning rather than promotion.
Why nowAmgen's shorter monitoring window moves IMDELLTRA towards community administration, Regeneron's PASATRU is a home-infusion launch, and Enspryng in MOGAD would be the first treatment in its disease. All three change operations, not just messaging.

02

Government pricing deals: turn the commitment into a work stream

What’s happeningPfizer has agreed to share overseas revenue with HHS and cut cancer prices in Kenya, Incyte has a CMS agreement on Jakafi, Amgen settled its most-favoured-nation dispute with Denmark, and a court has blocked imports of foreign-market Gilead products.
What to doEvery commitment creates reporting, pricing analytics and access-programme work that someone has to run. Offer to build and operate it: Medicaid and HTA reporting, price and access modelling, and localised patient and provider communications for each market.
Why nowThese are signed obligations with deadlines, not proposals — the work lands whether or not a partner is appointed.
Pfizer Incyte Amgen Gilead
03

Trust events: agree the playbook before the next one

What’s happeningAmgen has disclosed a patient-data breach, Pfizer has settled thousands of Depo-Provera claims, Regeneron faces securities suits and halted a trial after a safety review, and J&J has proposed a $5.5B talc settlement.
What to doOffer a standing capability rather than a one-off: compliant communications, patient and provider notification, controlled medical information, and the content operations behind them — scoped and pre-agreed so it can run within days.
Why nowEvery one of these companies has had an event in the last six weeks. The work is urgent when it arrives, which is the worst moment to select a partner.

Amgen
ACT NOW

Window  IMDELLTRA label change live; breach response under way

NUDGE’s read

Amgen is running three things at once: a label change that moves IMDELLTRA towards community administration, strong cardiovascular data for Repatha as a biosimilar threat forms, and the response to a patient-data breach. A new CFO is pressing execution and discipline, so proposals need a cost and outcome case.

What Indegene should do

1Oncology commercial, medical affairs and patient support — site-of-care planning, provider and patient education, and reimbursement navigation for the shorter IMDELLTRA monitoring window.
2Repatha commercial and market access — patient access, RWE and adherence support off the VESALIUS-CV mortality data and the wider EMA label — ahead of the Sandoz biosimilar.
3Privacy, patient access and IT security leads — patient notification and compliance communications for the breach, as a pre-agreed capability rather than a one-off.

Signals behind this

Gilead
BUILD

Window  Asia CAR-T build-out being decided

NUDGE’s read

Gilead is choosing between Korea, Japan and Taiwan for its first Asian CAR-T plant while pushing for wider Yescarta coverage in South Korea, and has won an injunction blocking imports of its foreign-market products. The opportunity is the Asia build-out; the near-term need is access and compliance support.

What Indegene should do

1Asia manufacturing, quality and market access leads — regulatory compliance, supply-chain and market-access support for the CAR-T site decision and the Korean coverage push.
2HIV market access, legal and communications — patient-access programme design and regulatory messaging following the import injunction.

Genentech
BUILD

Window  Enspryng MOGAD decision pending; pipeline and R&D expanding

NUDGE’s read

Genentech is buying and building capability, not standing still. Enspryng has Priority Review in MOGAD, an autoimmune disease with no approved treatment, so a decision lands inside this planning year. Behind it, a $1.5B+ collaboration with Earendil puts AI-designed bispecifics into the oncology pipeline and a new Boston centre adds cardiovascular, renal and metabolic research. The nearest revenue is the MOGAD launch — a rare-disease launch where the patients are scattered across neurology and ophthalmology and have to be found before they can be reached.

What Indegene should do

1Rare-disease launch readiness for Enspryng — map the MOGAD referral pathway and the neurologists and ophthalmologists who see these patients first, build the diagnosis and treatment education behind it, and have payer evidence and patient-support operations ready before the decision date rather than after it.
2Oncology medical affairs and data operations — position against the Earendil bispecific programme now — congress and publication planning, early scientific communications, and the data operations an AI-designed discovery pipeline generates — while the assets are pre-clinical and the partner list is still open.
3Account mapping across Genentech, Roche US and Boston — confirm who owns oncology, neuroscience and the new CVRM agenda after the Boston centre opens, and which service lines sit with Genentech versus Roche US, so proposals reach the budget holder rather than the brand.

Signals behind this

9 SepFDA granted Priority Review to Enspryng for MOGAD — an autoimmune disease with no approved treatments.

Incyte
ACT NOW

Window  CMS agreement live; post-Jakafi plan set out

NUDGE’s read

Incyte has agreed Jakafi Medicaid pricing with CMS, funded MINJUVI in Ontario and expanded OPZELURA in Australia — three access events in a month. Behind them sits a post-Jakafi plan to push five assets into Phase III, which is a launch-readiness agenda that has to be built now.

What Indegene should do

1Head of Market Access — operating support for the CMS agreement: Medicaid pricing analytics, payer engagement and the RWE behind it.
2Head of Commercial and the clinical-readout team — launch-readiness planning for the five post-Jakafi assets and the ESMO and ASH readouts.
3APAC commercial and regulatory affairs — registration, market access and launch orchestration for OPZELURA in Australia.

Pfizer is shipping an updated COMIRNATY in the US and Canada, financing a roughly $10B acquisition in obesity, and carrying $9.7B of cost reductions plus a large settlement programme. It has the most work in motion of any account here, and the least appetite for new spend — every proposal needs a cost case.

1US and Canada vaccines and regulatory communications — localised HCP and patient content, training and compliant materials for the XFG COMIRNATY rollout in both markets.
2M&A and obesity commercial leads — integration and launch communications for Metsera as the financing completes.
3Government affairs and pricing leads — the reporting and analytics behind the HHS revenue-share arrangement and the Kenya access programme.

Regeneron
ACT NOW

Window  PASATRU launching; November PDUFA ahead

NUDGE’s read

Regeneron has PASATRU approved and moving into home infusion, record quarterly sales across EYLEA HD, DUPIXENT and LIBTAYO, and a PDUFA in November. It is also managing a halted trial and securities suits, so the safest entry is launch operations rather than anything touching trial messaging.

What Indegene should do

1US commercial and rare-disease launch lead — HCP engagement, home-infusion operations, payer messaging and patient support for the PASATRU launch.
2US commercial and partnership lead — launch readiness and commercial analytics ahead of the November PDUFA and the cemdisiran catalysts.
3Pharmacovigilance and corporate communications — a safety-communications playbook after the TITAN trial halt, agreed before the next event.

Risks to manage

■Amgen — The breach touches clinical-trial and patient-support systems — expect security review of every vendor, including new ones.
■Regeneron — Securities suits over the LIBTAYO trial disclosures make every external claim sensitive; keep proposals clear of trial messaging.
■Pfizer — $9.7B of cost reductions through 2029 means procurement pressure — lead with cost-to-serve, not new spend.
■Genentech — The Enspryng decision date is not public, so launch timing has to be held as a range — build readiness that survives a slip, and keep the Earendil programme conversations scientific while the assets are pre-clinical.
